## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2021-04-06: Initial S-1 attaches form-of TRA as Exhibit 10.2
- 2021-07-27: TRA executed at IPO closing; filed July 30, 2021 as Exhibit 10.2 to IPO-close 8-K

#### Bain Capital merger and TRA waiver

- 2024-06-06: Amendment No. 1 to TRA executed concurrent with Bain Capital merger agreement; adds automatic-termination-at-Effective-Time language and waives all Tax Benefit Payments (including amounts already owed for 2021 and 2022 tax years)
- 2024-10-01: Bain merger Effective Time; TRA automatically terminates; pre-extinguishment liability written off without any cash TRA payment

## Explanation

PowerSchool Holdings, Inc. became the TRA obligor on July 27, 2021 at the closing of its Up-C IPO, with Severin Topco LLC, Vista Equity Partners funds, and Onex funds as the principal TRA Holders. The TRA paid beneficiaries 85% of cash tax savings from Section 754 basis step-ups arising from future LLC Unit exchanges, NOL carryforwards from the Vista Blocker I, Onex Blocker, and Vista Blocker II entities, and TRA-imputed interest. The recorded liability grew to roughly $419M (noncurrent + current) by June 30, 2024 with $22M already past due for the 2021 tax year. On June 6, 2024 PowerSchool executed Amendment No. 1 concurrent with the Bain Capital merger agreement; the amendment added automatic-termination-at-merger-close language to Section 4.2 and obtained a full waiver of all Tax Benefit Payments from the TRA Holders, with no substitute payment under the TRA. The merger closed on October 1, 2024, triggering automatic termination; the accrued liability was extinguished without any TRA-channel cash outflow. This was not a negotiated termination payment in the conventional sense; the TRA Holders were the same pre-merger controlling stockholders rolling into and supporting the Bain transaction, and the merger consideration evidently captured their full economic exit. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
